review-iarc-021.title: On the Generalization of Equivariance and Convolution in Neural Networks to the Action of Compact Groups

checks.location: Theorem 1, explicitly using Definition 3, concludes that all linear layers must be convolutions when all reachable layer activations transform equivariantly.
checks.claim: Theorem 1, explicitly using Definition 3, concludes that all linear layers must be convolutions when all reachable layer activations transform equivariantly.
checks.explanation: Equivariance of reachable activations constrains a later weight map only on the hidden states generated by preceding layers. It does not force that map to intertwine the group actions on the whole hidden feature space, as the convolution conclusion requires.
checks.demonstration:
Let $G=C_2$, with its nonidentity element acting on $X_0=X_1=G/\{e\}$ by the coordinate swap $P$. Let $X_2=G/G$ be a singleton, whose action is trivial. Use scalar real features, ReLU nonlinearities and
$$A_1=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad A_2=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
For every real input $x=(x_1,x_2)$, write $s=\max(0,x_1+x_2)$. The first activation is $(s,s)$ and the final activation is $s$. Swapping the input preserves $s$, so the first activation transforms by $P$ and the final activation is invariant, exactly as Definition 3 requires. The output is nonconstant.

However,
$$A_2P=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\end{pmatrix}\ne A_2.$$
Every convolution from $G$ to the singleton is invariant on all hidden inputs, whereas $A_2$ is not. Thus the network satisfies Definition 3 while its second linear map violates Definition 5. The failure occurs because the reachable hidden vectors lie on the diagonal: equivariance there does not determine the map away from that set.
checks.repair:
State the characterization for full-space layerwise intertwiners and specify the operator class. Let $G$ be compact Hausdorff, let the stabilizers be closed subgroups, and let feature maps be continuous functions on $G/H$ with finite-dimensional channels. Assume each linear layer has a continuous integral kernel with respect to the invariant probability measure. For an input space $G/H$ and output space $G/K$,
$$[Af](y)=\int_{G/H}\kappa(y,x)f(x)\,d\mu(x).$$
The identity $AL_g=L_gA$ holds exactly when $\kappa(gy,gx)=\kappa(y,x)$. An invariant kernel can be obtained by Haar averaging, which leaves an already equivariant operator unchanged. Defining $\chi(v)=\kappa(vK,H)$ gives $\chi(hvk)=\chi(v)$ for $h\in H$ and $k\in K$, and
$$[Af](gK)=\int_G\chi(v)f(gv^{-1}H)\,dv.$$
Conversely, every continuous filter with these subgroup invariances gives an intertwining operator. This proves the compact-group convolution characterization under explicit regularity assumptions.

For ReLU networks in this kernel class, one can also repair the network-level conclusion by asserting the existence of an equivalent convolutional realization. If the original network satisfies Definition 3, average each linear layer over group conjugations. On a reachable input, every conjugated preactivation has the same ReLU output. A positive output forces all those preactivations to equal that output; a zero output makes them all nonpositive. Averaging therefore preserves the output. Replacing the layers successively preserves every activation, depth and feature dimension, while the averaged kernels are convolutions. This proves existence of a convolutional replacement; it does not make the original weights convolutional.
checks.scope: The original parameter-level necessity claim remains false. The corrected compact-group theorem requires full-space layerwise equivariance and continuous integral kernels. Under ReLU, the original operational equivariance additionally gives an equivalent convolutional realization with identical activations. The kernel assumption is automatic on finite spaces but excludes singular operators such as the identity on $C(S^1)$; allowing finite measure filters extends the characterization to bounded equivariant operators. The replacement argument is not asserted for arbitrary nonlinearities.

review-neurips-2026-153240.issueTitle: Restricted nonlinear ANMs need not have the proposed conditional rank gap
review-neurips-2026-153240.plainExplanation: Smooth restricted nonlinear and linear non-Gaussian additive-noise models can give rank one to both a sink and a nonsink at every conditioning value. The nonlinear rank-gap guarantee therefore needs an additional nondegeneracy condition. In the linear example, pooling conditional covariances restores the rank gap, so the practical averaged test is not refuted. The estimation appendix also needs the standard conversion from a noise predictor to the smoothed score.

checks.location: Appendix C, Positivity of W_h; Eq. (22)
checks.claim: Every admitted strictly convex C2 generator gives strictly positive update weights.
checks.explanation: Twice differentiable strict convexity does not require strictly positive curvature at every point. An allowed generator can therefore give a zero update weight at ratio one even when the model's preference ratios are incorrect.
checks.demonstration:
Take \(h(t)=(t-1)^4\) on \((0,\infty)\). Its derivative \(4(t-1)^3\) is strictly increasing, so \(h\) is strictly convex, but \(h''(1)=0\). Equation (40) therefore gives
\[W_h(1)=1^2h''(1)+1^{-1}h''(1)=0.\]
This zero need not indicate a correctly fitted model. Fix one prompt and two responses. Give the two preference orientations probabilities \(3/4\) and \(1/4\), as realized by a Bradley–Terry reward difference \(\log3\). Let both safety labels be equal and let both the model and reference policies be uniform. The model ratio is then one in either orientation, while the data ratios are \(1/3\) and \(3\).

Because \(h(1)=h'(1)=0\), the ratio-matching Bregman divergence is
\[\frac34 B_h(1/3\|1)+\frac14 B_h(3\|1)=\frac34\left(\frac23\right)^4+\frac14(2)^4=\frac{112}{27}>0.\]
Nevertheless both update weights vanish. This refutes strict positivity for the admitted generator class; it does not refute the particular positive-curvature generators or the strict-convexity argument identifying a minimizing ratio.
checks.repair: For strictly positive weights, require \(h^{\prime\prime}(t)>0\) on the relevant ratio domain, and verify it for each generator. Otherwise state nonnegative weights with possible zeros and analyze the consequences.
checks.scope: Universal positivity fails over the stated class. The named positive-curvature generators and strict-convex Bregman argmin identification remain valid.
